report:
## Conclusion: The evidence contradicts your view — denosumab does reduce vertebral fracture risk

The strongest evidence comes from the FREEDOM trial, a large, international, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis. It found that denosumab (60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months) reduced the risk of new radiographic vertebral fractures by approximately 68% compared with placebo over 36 months, along with reductions in hip fracture (~40%) and nonvertebral fracture (~20%) (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493). Independent NNT analysis of this trial data puts the number needed to treat to prevent one vertebral fracture at around 21–15–25 over 3 years, consistent with a clinically meaningful and statistically robust effect (https://thennt.com/nnt/denosumab-reducing-risk-fractures-postmenopausal-women/). Additional randomized trials in other populations, such as the DIRECT trial in Japanese men and postmenopausal women, similarly found vertebral fracture risk reductions of roughly 66% (https://www.academia.edu/14092057/Fracture_Risk_Reduction_with_Denosumab_in_Japanese_Postmenopausal_Women_and_Men_with_Osteoporosis_Denosumab_fracture_Intervention_RandomizEd_placebo_Controlled_Trial_DIRECT_).

The one caveat, which is real and important, concerns discontinuation rather than efficacy during treatment: stopping denosumab causes a rapid rebound in bone turnover and is associated with a 3- to 5-fold increased risk of vertebral fractures, sometimes multiple fractures, within months of the last dose (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7796169/). This has prompted regulatory warnings and recommendations for transition therapy after discontinuation, but it does not negate the drug's protective effect while patients remain on treatment.

**Bottom line:** High-quality RCT evidence clearly shows denosumab reduces vertebral fracture risk during active treatment. The main safety concern is fracture rebound after stopping the drug, not lack of efficacy.
